benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Firmed to about $114.80 on 28 Oct (Trading Economics), up roughly 0.8% on the day and about 4% w/w, as the Ras Tanura fire's damage stayed unconfirmed a day on and the Houthis' East-West pipeline/Riyadh airport claims remained unverified, keeping a geopolitical premium in the market. Week-ago is this site's 21 Oct reading, exactly 7 days earlier.

benchmarks.label: Henry Hub
benchmarks.note: Rebounded to about $3.07 on 28 Oct (Trading Economics), up roughly 2% on the day and 7% w/w, though still within its recent range; pre-crisis is the EIA spot price on 27 Feb (FRED). US LNG feedgas and exports are near records, but the US price stays largely insulated from the Hormuz and Red Sea turmoil.

note: Brent and WTI firmed on 28 October, a day after a fire broke out near Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura export terminal following an attack; the extent of the damage remains unconfirmed, and the Houthis' East-West pipeline and Riyadh airport claims remain unverified. TTF extended its rally to a fresh 2026 high above €97/MWh on tight European winter gas supply, while JKM eased slightly from Monday's high. Henry Hub rebounded but stays largely insulated from the Gulf turmoil.
